hook.line: On-screen text only: this is how old generative AI looked.
hook.visual: A greyscale, distorted anime face with glowing red eyes fills the frame under a centred white caption; it dissolves into the next image around 1.9 s.

beats.what: Creepy greyscale AI anime girl with red eyes; the fixed caption sits mid-frame for the whole video.
Crossfade to a red-haired figure with melted black eyes; the slideshow rhythm is set.
Teal-haired character with hollow black eye sockets, double-exposed during the dissolve.
Off-pattern image: a distorted photo of a child with a dog breaks the anime run.
Pink-haired girl whose face is a blank white mask.
Two girls hugging, one with empty black eyes and a stretched mouth.
Final image: a full-frame teal-haired figure with black eye holes, held to the end so it loops back to the first frame.

why_it_works: One fixed line of text frames every image, so the viewer needs no audio and every new picture is its own small payoff.
Each image is uncanny (empty eyes, melted faces), so the viewer keeps watching to see the next unsettling one and often loops; the measured loop score is 0.536.
Nostalgia plus 'look how far AI has come' invites comments comparing old and new AI images.
weaknesses: No cuts are detected (0 cuts, a single 15 s shot) because every change is a slow dissolve, so the pace feels soft.
The caption sits in the middle band (caption_band_share middle 0.729) on top of the faces, covering the eyes that are the point of each image.
No voice and no CTA; the account gets no follow from the views.
for_robert: Use the 'before vs now' reveal of old AI output as a quick cutaway in a reel (Fred reacting in horror to a melted early-AI face), but hard-cut each image rather than slow dissolves.
